items.title: feat(laptop-agent): implement the #5759 /files/* transfer routes
items.body: Closes the daemon half of **#10355** step 1 (design #5759). ## Problem `fleet proxy get/put` shipped client-side in #5759, but the laptop-agent daemon never implemented the `/files/*` routes, so the verbs fail live: ``` fleet: daemon /files/stat: no such route ``` Every file still crosses as base64-in-exec (~33% tax, ~1 MiB cap, no resume) or one-off SSH-stdin scripts. ## What this does Implements the daemon side on the **canonical source** `pkgs/laptop-agent/src/laptop_agent.py`, following the route semantics of the shipped client's in-memory fake daemon — that fake is the protocol's oracle. | route | behaviour | |---|---| | `/files/stat` | `exists`/`type`/`size`/`mtime`; optional whole-file `sha256` | | `/files/begin` | create the deterministic temp, keep an existing one (resume), record a pending `mode` | | `/files/write` | offset-idempotent chunk write; conflicting rewrite and offset-beyond-end refused; fsync | | `/files/commit` | verify whole-file sha256, apply mode, atomic `os.replace`, fsync dir | | `/files/abort` | remove the temp | | `/files/read` | bounded chunk read with `eof`, `size`, `mtime` | Design invariants preserved: - **deterministic temps** `..fleet-part-` (mirrors the client's `temp_path_for`) - **atomic publish** at commit, so partial content is *never* visible at the destination path - **resume** purely from the temp's stat'd size - a **transfer body cap** sized for the client's 2 MiB base64 chunks — the existing `/exec` `MAX_BODY` (1 MiB) is too small for a chunk body, so `/files/*` reads under its own cap plus a per-chunk cap. Path validation (non-empty, no NUL) and mode validation (`0..0o7777`) match the client's bounds; confinement is deliberately none, as the design states (the daemon already runs arbitrary commands as the same user). ## Tests - `tests/test_files_routes.py` — 17 hermetic cases: multi-chunk round trip, destination-untouched-until-commit, commit hash mismatch keeps temp *and* destination, resume from a partial temp, offset-idempotent replay, conflict/offset refusals, abort, mode at commit, path/mode validation, 2 MiB chunk body (proves the `MAX_BODY` gap is handled). - `tests/parity_roundtrip.py` — extended to drive every `/files/*` route in the exact client wire shape. - Full suite: **82 tests pass** (65 pre-existing + 17 new). `black --check` clean. Live acceptance run (hermetic daemon on a scratch port, 100 MiB): ``` PUT 100MiB: 1.4s sha256 identical=True GET 100MiB: 1.0s sha256 identical=True daemon-stated-match=True mid-flight: destination exists? False (must be False) resume point: 2097152 bytes kill-resume completed, sha identical= True temp gone= True ``` ## Not in this PR The deployment restart of the shared `laptop-agent.service` and subsequent steps of #10355 (copy verb, SCP-style addressing, script migrations, throughput close-out) stay on the issue. This PR lands the daemon code and its verification, which is the blocker four prior lanes deferred. ## Verification ``` python3 -m unittest discover -s pkgs/laptop-agent/tests # 82 pass python3 pkgs/laptop-agent/tests/parity_roundtrip.py # RESULT: ALL PASS ``` --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added authenticated file transfer capabilities, including uploads, downloads, and file metadata checks. * Large transfers can be sent in chunks and resumed after interruption. Uploads are verified before the destination file is updated, helping prevent incomplete or corrupted files from replacing existing files.

items.title: feat(fleet-proxy): fleet proxy get/put client v1 (#5759)
items.body: Implements the developing-today/code client half of #5759 (`fleet proxy get` / `fleet proxy put`, v1) — queue task 14003. The daemon `/files/*` routes are separately owned and stay untouched; #5759 stays open until the API is deployed end-to-end (per the task packet). ## What lands - **New `fleet-proxy::files` module** — the client for the design's daemon RPC (`stat` / `begin` / `write` / `commit` / `abort` / `read`) over the existing session-broker channel (framed `Request`/`Response` to the laptop-agent service on port 4799, token by file name — the shape `fleet-secrets`' broker source established). - 2 MiB chunks, whole-file SHA-256 verified at commit (put) and before the local rename (get), deterministic transfer temps (`..fleet-part-`) with resume on both sides, offset-idempotent writes, `--mode` handling (put defaults to the local file's mode; stdin defaults to 0644), recursive `put -r` (client-side walk, symlinks skipped and said so), stdin/stdout streaming forms (`put -` spools locally because `begin` needs size + hash up front; `get -` streams and verifies at the end). - SHA-256 and base64 are implemented in-module, std-only, so the verbs can live in `proxy-connect` — compiled into every variant including the size-gated connect builds — without new dependencies. Oracle-named tests cover both codecs (FIPS 180-4 and RFC 4648 vectors). - **Registry + dispatch**: `get`/`put` join the proxy domain's subcommands and route to `Capability::ProxyConnect`; usage/help text updated. - **Tests (hermetic fake daemon)**: an in-memory implementation of the protocol plus a framed fake-broker socket server drive the real client code — multi-chunk put/get round trip (byte-identical), resume continuing from the temp size with only the remaining chunk re-sent, offset idempotency vs conflicting rewrite, commit refusing a hash mismatch and keeping the temp, get verifying before rename, chunk-plan tiling, arg/mode parsing. Results: fleet-proxy 83/83 (10 new), fleet-registry 5/5, fleet 27/27, and the `--no-default-features` (connect) build's files tests 10/10. ## Deferred, explicitly (packet allowance) - `get -r`: the v1 daemon protocol has no directory-listing route, so a recursive download cannot be enumerated. The verb answers with a usage error naming the deferral instead of guessing; the follow-up is recorded on #5759. ## Not yet verified - Live end-to-end against the real daemon: the `/files/*` routes do not exist on the deployed laptop-agent daemon yet (daemon side separately owned). Verification here is the hermetic fake-daemon suite specified by the packet. - The D7 connect size gate (≤ 2 MiB): a local release build of the connect variant (`cargo build --release -p fleet --no-default-features`) measures 926,664 bytes with the verbs included; smoke.sh under the Nix builds in CI remains the authoritative check. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: ci(id): raise the e2e nightly timeout from 90 to 300 minutes

labels.name: audit:no-issue
labels.description: No spawning issue; judged on stated intent

items.body: ## What `id-e2e-nightly.yml`: the check job's `timeout-minutes` goes 90 → 300, with the evidence recorded in the file header. ## Why The nightly has produced no result in a week. Every run from 2026-11-16 through 2026-11-21 concluded **cancelled** with a job runtime of almost exactly 90 minutes: - run 44919101712 (2026-11-21): job 15:25:27Z → 16:55:51Z = **90m24s** - run 44771169615 (2026-11-20): created→updated ≈ 92m That is this job's own timeout killing the check mid-run — not a test failure, not a successor run cancelling it (the next schedule is 24h later), and not the #8866 pattern. The suite budgets alone exceed 90 minutes serially (nixos-integration `globalTimeout` 3600s, nixos-playwright-e2e 1200s) before any build time, and a cold or throttled store cache (see the #774 note in this same file) pushes the total well past 90. ## Effect #1372 and #1374 are both waiting on one completed full-check run to validate fixes that are already on main; both are now `status/blocked` with this as the recorded blocker. The first nightly that runs to completion after this merges unblocks them. ## Verification Workflow-only change; per `.github/ci-policy.md` the done check is the next scheduled (or dispatched) nightly run completing with a real conclusion instead of a 90-minute cancellation. Refs #1372, #1374 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

The hatch copies stay in place — they are the deployed seat copies' kin — and gain canonical-pointer headers in a companion hatch PR. Nothing is deleted anywhere. ### Mapping | Hatch source | Canonical home (this PR) | Notes | |---|---|---| | `tools/gh-post` | `pkgs/gh-fleet/gh-post` | The fleet-wide GitHub posting tool; `pkgs/gh-fleet/` was a stub (`default.nix` only) | | `tools/test-gh-post-app-leg.py` | `pkgs/gh-fleet/test-gh-post-app-leg.py` | App-leg regression test (code#7935); passes against the copied `gh-post` | | `tools/laptop-agent.py` | `pkgs/fleet/laptop-agent.py` | Fleet-shell client (Cloudflare-tunnel primary, tailnet fallback) | | `tools/laptop-agent-broker.py` | `pkgs/fleet/laptop-agent-broker.py` | Warm-connection broker for the client; no code counterpart existed | | `tools/runtime-db-export/` (whole tree, 24 files incl. README + milestone specs) | `pkgs/fleet/runtime-db-export/` | Runtime-DB → Turso/Postgres export, beside `pkgs/fleet/migrations/` | | `tools/provider-usage/{check-usage.py, reconcile.py, test_reconcile.py}` | `pm-stack/provider-usage/` | New sibling dir under pm-stack: these are standalone Python keeper tools whose snapshot/registry outputs feed the quota plane. Not `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/` — that dir is the aggregator app's bun-run TypeScript entry points | | `tools/quota-check/turso-mirror-read.py` | `pm-stack/quota-check/turso-mirror-read.py` | Quota-mirror reader (code#6828: per-DB libsql HTTP reads, tokens by name). pm-stack rather than `scripts/` because its subject is the quota store and it belongs to the quota plane; hatch family name kept | | `tools/oc-attach.py` | `scripts/oc-attach.py` | OpenChamber attach helper (the fleet-machine watchdog's session check consumes this path) | | `tools/oc-attach` | `scripts/oc-attach` | In hatch this is an absolute symlink to the seat's live file; here it is a **relative** symlink → `oc-attach.py` (mode 120000) | | `tools/oc-attach.md` | `scripts/oc-attach.md` | Helper doc, travels with the tool | ### Not copied — already canonical in code (found during reconciliation) | Hatch source | Already in code | Evidence | |---|---|---| | `tools/laptop-agent-daemon.py` | `pkgs/laptop-agent/src/laptop_agent.py` | code#10131 vendored the **reconciled union** daemon (2026-11-17) and #5759 added the `/files/*` routes. The service/timer are expressed as the registry's `timer` field (onCalendar `*:0/5`, persistent); hatch's hand-copied units + installer are the superseded pre-registry source. Pointer-only in hatch | ### Reconcile verdicts — the duplicated-and-diverged set (`pkgs/fleet/` already canonical) | File | Verdict | |---|---| | `lane-claim.sh` | Whitespace only (redirect spacing `>`). Identical semantics — no change | | `lane-handoff.sh` | Formatting only (one assignment line split into three) — no change | | `enqueue-when-green.sh` | Formatting only (case-statement rewrap) — no change | | `turso-exec.py` | **AST-identical** to code's copy; the textual diff is black-style rewrapping in both directions — no change | | `repo-task-v1.schema.json` | Code's copy is the newer superset: nothing hatch-only. Code-only additions: `implementation_repo`, `required_budget_minutes`, `allOf`; two `description` strings updated with the #4919 defaulting behaviour — no change | | `fleet-build-lock` | Code's copy is a **strict superset**: the diff is 143 added lines, zero hatch-only lines (the cargo target-pool leasing block) — no change | | `fleet-fetch.py` | Functionally identical; the one hatch-only content was documentation — the module docstring's migration **History paragraph**, which code's copy had condensed to two lines. **Folded in this PR** (hunk below). items.title: feat(fleet): laptop-agent domain with transport ladder and verbs

labels.name: audit:completed-later
labels.description: Gap completed by later merged PR

items.body: Implements the fleet laptop-agent domain from #10796: a new `fleet-laptop-agent` crate with the verbs `exec`, `run`, `poll`, `kill`, `jobs`, `health` and `fetch`, over the transport ladder broker → Cloudflare → Tailscale → SSH. Wired into `fleet` behind the `laptop-agent` feature. ## What mirrors the Python client - X-Agent-Token header only, read from the token file. - Trip ids and the trip-log record shape (same field order). - Deadline with best-effort `/exec//cancel`; 1 MiB per-stream capture cap with truncation announced. - Primary-checkout guards (code#10095): refuses git mutations on a primary checkout and jobs whose cwd is a primary; `LAPTOP_AGENT_PRIMARY_OK=1` overrides. - Cloudflare Access credential comes from the fleet secret `cloudflare.access-laptop-agent`; the value is never printed or logged. ## Ladder rules - An absent or unsent leg falls through. - A sent non-idempotent request is never replayed. - A sent idempotent request may fall through. ## Not in this PR - **SSH leg** is a named stub (always absent) because `~/tools/laptop-ssh-real.sh` is not present in this sandbox. - **Python client untouched.** `~/tools/laptop-agent.py` and `laptop-ssh.sh` are not re-pointed; parity against a live laptop has not been run here. - **`fetch`** reads the daemon's `GET /file` in 1 MiB ranges and checks sha256 against a remote `shasum -a 256` run through `/exec`. The daemon has no upload route, so the push direction of the hash-checked transfer is not implemented. ## Tests `cargo test -p fleet-laptop-agent` (19 unit tests) passes under cargo-target-broker. `cargo build -p fleet --features laptop-agent` builds. Parity proofs (round-trip exec per leg, hash-checked transfer both ways, forced-leg-down fallback, trip-log equivalence) still need a live laptop and are tracked on #10796. Refs #10796 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added a laptop-agent command-line tool for checking health, listing and managing jobs, running commands, polling results, and fetching files. - Added multiple connection options with automatic fallback, plus safeguards against running jobs in primary Git checkouts. - File downloads are verified before being saved.
